tier_reason: arma.sourceforge.net/speed.html is a first-party page with approximate speed-up labels over IT++ and Newmat, a code extract only (no full harness), GCC 4.3.0 with no flags and a Core2 Duo without model number; not A, and the >50x rows (77x, 1086x) with unstated flags are capped at C anyway.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Approximate speed-ups over IT++/Newmat as labelled on the page: add two matrices 4x4 15x/10x, 100x100 3.5x/same speed; add four matrices 4x4 15x/10x, 100x100 6x/1.5x; multiply four matrices (100x80..40x20) 2.5x/10x and (1000x800..400x200) 2.5x/20x; submatrix row copy 4x4 16x/44x, 100x100 2x/4.5x; multi-operation expression trans(p)*inv(diagmat(q))*r 4x4 77x/23x, 100x100 1086x/5x (the 'add three matrices' plots carry no speed-up labels).
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from a Core2 Duo (2 GHz, 2 MB cache) / Linux 2.6.26 / GCC 4.3.0 setup from Armadillo's early releases; compiler flags and exact CPU model are not stated, only a timing-loop code extract (not the full harness) is shown, and results are graphs with 'approximate speed-up' labels. The baselines are two older, less-used C++ matrix libraries (IT++, Newmat), not BLAS or Eigen, so the record's blas-lapack category baseline is not what was beaten; Armadillo is an expression-template front end (it links BLAS/LAPACK for heavy kernels, general knowledge, not stated on this page), and the big wins come from avoiding temporaries and reordering chained expressions (the page says the 1086x case compiles into a single loop without temporaries), not from faster kernels. Third-party snippets (not opened) suggest BLAS-linked Eigen can beat Armadillo on 512x512 multiplication, so the claim is not universal. The repository moved from gitlab.com/conradsnicta/armadillo-code to gitlab.com/armadillo-lib/armadillo-code (GitLab API 301 to project 6604173, default branch 15.6.x).

notes: Every speed-up on the page matches the record (record omitted the 4x4 add-four row, added). Metadata checked via the GitLab API: Apache-2.0, 268 stars, not archived or forked, last commit on default branch 15.6.x 2026-10-02; canonical repo is gitlab.com/armadillo-lib/armadillo-code (repo_url cannot be corrected here, consider an override). Shortcomings: old first-party page, weak baselines (IT++/Newmat), no flags, wins are expression fusion not kernels.

tier_reason: doc/bbf.rst gives first-party `time` output for bbfdetect (real 0m9.304s) versus OpenCV's default face detector (real 0m27.977s) on the author's computer, with no CPU model, compiler, flags, OpenCV version or OpenCV program; the bbfdetect side is public (bin/bbfdetect.c) but the method is partial, so C.

corrections.caveats: doc/bbf.rst opens with a Deprecated notice: BBF 'is no longer considered either fast or accurate' for face detection as of libccv 0.7 and was to be removed after 0.7 in favour of SCD; the code (lib/ccv_bbf.c, bin/bbfdetect.c) is still in the repo. The speed numbers are a first-party doc from the OpenCV 2.x era with no CPU model, compiler or flags and no script beyond the shown shell commands, so the tier stops at C. The timed run includes image decoding and output for both programs, the OpenCV program and version are not named, and OpenCV ran with default settings, not necessarily equivalent to bbfdetect's scale and neighbour parameters. Accuracy trade on CMU test sets A/B/C: BBF 82.97% with 12 false alarms versus OpenCV 86.69% with 15; on FDDB (doc/scd.rst) at about 250 false positives BBF reaches 66.27% versus OpenCV frontal 45.18%. doc/scd.rst also reports SCD about 2x slower than BBF (addams-family.png 381 ms vs 182 ms) and OpenCV about 3x slower than BBF single-threaded. ccv's dpm.rst shows OpenCV's HOG pedestrian detector 4.34 times faster than ccv's DPM, and the convnet doc says it chooses correctness over speed, so the claim covers only the BBF face detector. Licence: code BSD-3-Clause (COPYING), but ./doc, ./samples (including the trained face cascade) and ./site are CC BY 4.0; bundled kissfft (BSD) and metal-cpp (Apache-2.0).

notes: Numbers match doc/bbf.rst exactly (about 3.0x derived from page data) and the 3x statement is in doc/scd.rst. Metadata via github.com: 7.2k stars, not archived or a fork, default branch unstable, last commit 2026-10-07. Main shortcoming to record: BBF is self-declared deprecated ('no longer considered either fast or accurate'), and the benchmark is an undocumented single `time` run against an unnamed OpenCV build.

tier_reason: The README tables (glog write speed, spdlog seconds for 1 million logs, rapidjson microseconds) are first-party with no compiler, flags, CPU models or library versions, and only the co/log and co/json halves of the harness exist (test/log.cc, test/jbm.cc), with no glog, spdlog or rapidjson code; the >50x rows (112.5x, 151.3x) with unstated flags are capped at C.

corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers only: no compiler, flags, library versions or CPU models. The benchmark/ directory (atomic, idgen, main, mem, rand, string, time, xtoa) has no log test; test/log.cc -perf times 1 million single-threaded log::info calls and reports separately the time to the in-memory cache and the time after log::close() flushes to file, and test/jbm.cc times co/json only (str() measured once, parse averaged over -n runs), so neither the glog, spdlog nor rapidjson side, nor the 2-8 thread runs, can be reproduced from the repo, and the README does not say whether co/log's figures are cache time or file time. co/log buffers and flushes asynchronously (per test/log.cc), while spdlog's configuration (sink, sync or async mode, version) is not stated, so the spdlog rows may compare async against sync logging. The glog rows are write speeds on different storage (HDD/SSD) and OS combinations. Coost also publishes co/json vs rapidjson (twitter.json minified, stringify/parse in microseconds: win 569/924 vs 2089/2495, mac 783/1097 vs 1289/1658, linux 468/764 vs 1359/1070, claimed 1.4-3.6x) with the same tier-C caveats.

notes: All log and json numbers match readme.md. Metadata via github.com: MIT, 4.2k stars, 592 forks, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-09-28. Shortcomings: no baseline harness in the repo (only co/log and co/json halves in test/), unstated spdlog/glog configuration and likely async-vs-sync comparison, no hardware or flags.
